channel.title: The Diff: AI dev news, only what is verified
channel.description: Every issue of The Diff. What went viral in AI dev tools, and what nobody has noticed yet.

item.title: No. 053: 2035 came early - a full Linux desktop boots in a browser tab. A 945-point essay: your agent works for its parent company, not you.
item.description: trynix.dev runs 300,000+ Nix packages on unkernel, Linux compiled to WebAssembly - windows, sound, GL, networking, Firefox-in-Firefox. Harley's essay on agent loyalty. Anthropic closed at $81.91, below its $83 IPO price, with the Amodeis' $561M sale in the filings; a Polymarket wallet bought Huang's return 89 minutes before Trump's post (+1,438%); Alpoge says the 250,000 pages were a joke. Plus: Bonsai 2.5, a 27B agentic model in 5.9 GB.

item.title: No. 052: Jensen Huang is Nvidia's CEO again - unanimous vote, Washington's input, +31% close. Z.ai's GLM-5.4 loops a 750B model's layers twice.
item.description: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang after government input - stock closed +31%; the investigation continues, testimony Dec 1-3. Z.ai's GLM-5.4 loop transformer runs 28 layers twice at 750B, claiming 2T-3T-class coding (vendor numbers). The Riemann certification finished every check but one overnight. Meta's Wang answered OpenAI's limits proposal without signing. Plus: a 27B coding model in an 8.4 GB file.

item.title: No. 051: OpenAI's chief scientist publishes the internal perplexity curve - and proposes an industry speed limit. The human Riemann proof gets its own verification race.
item.description: OpenAI's Jakub Pachocki discloses the internal log-perplexity trajectory - GPT-3.5 ~0.99, GPT-4 ~0.91, below 0.8 now, ~0.76 when the math breakthroughs started, new capabilities expected at ~0.68-0.7 - and proposes shared transparency standards, joint evaluations and common development limits labs would not cross until monitoring catches up; a possible pretraining avalanche "as soon as 2027." John Baez publishes the first readable sketch of Masullo's 940-page human proof, flagging problems already found; a community Lean formalization runs on GitHub with a public progress map; Rubinstein and Adriazola reconstruct the Alpöge-Claude proof for humans. GL.iNet's exploited cloud flaw infected routers and KVMs - check for `crond -i /tmp/.log` and install the security firmware. The last two RH kernel replays still run at MIT. Inkling 2 Mini, three days old, already headlines beginner guides to local AI.

item.title: No. 050: The Lean community certifies the Claude Riemann proof. Someone shrunk Inkling 2 Mini to 5.4GB.
item.description: The Lean and Mathlib communities, endorsed by the Lean FRO, certify Alpöge’s Claude-assisted Riemann Hypothesis proof: statement and proof correct, independent kernels accept the 61.6GB export, two checks still running. A one-person quant shrinks Inkling 2 Mini to 5.38GB for Apple Silicon, beating quants twice its size. The rival human GRH proof gets a titled rebuttal - from an author who also claims RH is independent of ZFC. OpenRouter off-boards three inference providers, pulls 125 endpoints from zero-data-retention. GPT-6.1 Terra lands at half of 6.1 Sol’s price.

item.title: No. 049: An Anthropic mathematician says Claude proved the Riemann Hypothesis. Inkling 2 Mini loops a 26B onto your laptop.
item.description: Levent Alpöge’s announcement on his own site: a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, extending to GRH, formalized in Lean (14 archives; a readable write-up “hit 250,000+ pages”); Scott Aaronson counts 17.4M lines and bets it stands. Rival human GRH draft by Masullo wobbled within eight hours, gaps flagged with AI help. ANT closed day two at $88.91 (-8.5%) with the greenshoe exercised ($119.5B total raised incl. private placement). Inkling 2 Mini: looped transformer, 26.4B total/3.4B active, ~20GB, open weights, DeepSWE 48.2% and SWE-bench Verified 79.2% (lab-reported), airplane-mode demo. A 27B model rewrites its own weights, no gradients.

item.title: No. 048: Anthropic’s first day: $111.50 open, $97.17 close. GPT-6.2’s price cut meets its first backlash.
item.description: AP-verified open ($111.50) and close ($97.17, +17%) for ANT’s record debut; Reuters’ $2 trillion intraday mark; TechCrunch’s $2B founders cash-out. GPT-6.2 Astra at $8/$40 (20% cut) and Sol at $2/$10 per OpenAI’s post; Artificial Analysis #3 for Astra vs a SimpleBench regression below the human baseline. Claude solves two black-hole physics problems; California subpoenas Nvidia; Genie 4 live in Project Genie.

item.title: No. 047: Anthropic priced at $83 - the biggest IPO on record trades today. Google’s Gemini 4 Neon at $3 a million input tokens.
item.description: Anthropic’s official pricing: $83.00 per share, above the $70-78 range, upsized to 980,000,000 shares; NPR reports a record $81.3B raise; ANT debuts on Nasdaq today, opening price still ahead at send time. Gemini 4 Neon: $3/M input, $15/M output, 1M context, Google-claimed #1 on the AA Coding Agent Index; VentureBeat’s Opus 5.5 framing flagged as theirs. Nvidia’s first all-hands since Huang’s resignation; Tencent’s Hy4 flash open release; Claude Meetings still in monitoring.

item.title: No. 046: Nvidia doubles revenue to $115.8B. Board: Huang is not coming back.
item.description: Nvidia Q3 FY27 official: revenue $115.8B, up 103% Y/Y; Q4 guided at $130B assuming no China data-center compute revenue; Vera Rubin NVL72 shipped and in GA at Google Cloud and OCI. Board chair Jones on the call: the board unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation and does not intend to reinstate him; Heidrick & Struggles retained for the CEO search; new National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. SEC probe remains WSJ reporting. Anthropic expected to price its 825,000,000-share IPO today at $70-78, reportedly top of range or above per unnamed sources; trading expected Thursday under ANT. Claude Code 2.1.327; Meetings restored for Team; second Apple sign-in incident resolved.

item.title: No. 045: Alibaba’s Qwen4-Max: 2.4T parameters, a million-token context. BIS targets remote chip access.
item.description: Qwen4-Max live on the API: 2.4T MoE, 71B active, 1M context, $0.075 per million cached input tokens, Code Arena #6 per Alibaba - every vendor number flagged; BIS says its interim final rule targets remote access to restricted chips via third-country data centers, written at Treasury and NSC direction; Lutnick to testify Dec 10 per CBS; Claude Code 2.1.326; Claude Meetings still paused for Team plans.

item.title: No. 044: A $3 Arduino, two coding agents and a 1994 Jeep ECU. The brawl over Nvidia’s next CEO.
item.description: Muhammad Zulali’s xj-scanner - a 1991-95 Jeep ECU read by an AI agent through a $3 Arduino Nano, video verified, repo public; the fight over Nvidia’s next CEO: FT’s comeback report and the Rene Haas approach vs the board’s statement, Bessent’s “dramatic shakeup” demand and Megaspeed’s first denial, with Tuesday’s earnings call as checkpoint; Anthropic’s IPO book six times oversubscribed per Reuters, Opus 5.5 now the default on paid plans and Fable 5.2’s Python brushstrokes.

item.title: No. 043: Vibe-coded Lovable apps expose passports and 200,000 private chats. WSJ: Huang’s “avalanche” and the CFO who replaces him.
item.description: Crissy Field’s 159,041-project sample of Lovable apps - 7,403 sites (30% of those checked) returning records with emails via the public Supabase key, with the authors’ own caveats, plus Lovable’s security guide and the five-minute RLS audit; the WSJ’s account of Nvidia’s financing spree, the halved $250B OpenAI backstop and the verified Stevens Form 4; Google’s /teamwork proof claims, Decider v1.3’s independent Decision Index 70, GLM-5.3 on two DGX Stations and PyPI’s security signals.

item.title: No. 042: Anthropic went down twice in a day - and some scheduled runs never happened. Perplexity publishes how it trains Decider v1.3.
item.description: The verified timeline of Anthropic’s two Friday incidents plus a third still recovering Saturday, with the skipped scheduled runs in Anthropic’s own words; Perplexity’s Decider v1.3 decision model (Qwen3.8-27B, gated weights, free OpenRouter tier, Locate spans); Claude Code’s five parallel-agent patterns, 2.1.325’s security fix on day 8, and Brave Search API x402 payments.

item.title: No. 041: Gemini 4 Hydrogen beats Argon on the index at $1.50/$7.50 — and Orchestrator swaps models mid-task. Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, effective immediately.
item.description: Google’s Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Antigravity’s Orchestrator with Artificial Analysis’s overnight measurements ($3.16 per task, verbosity #76/77); Nvidia’s board statement on Huang’s resignation, Kress interim, Jones chair, and the unmentioned investigation; Claude Code 2.1.323’s Code Mode with the settings.local.json fix still absent; AA’s Decision Index on Gemini Decision 1; Anthropic’s IPO portal and reported Nov 18/19 dates.

item.title: No. 040: Google’s Gemini Decision 1 answers 1,000 questions in one pass — no text, output free. GitLab ships the settings.local.json block Anthropic hasn’t.
item.description: Google’s Decisions API and Gemini Decision 1 specs with Simon Willison’s same-day video test; GitLab’s push-rule defense for the exposed settings files against Anthropic’s unchanged changelog; United’s AI-agent booking ban; Fable 5.2’s cost frontier at Plotly and the DualEntry accounting regression; Anthropic IPO oversubscription reporting.

item.title: No. 039: Anthropic answers the exposed-secrets report on Hacker News — prototypes, no shipped fix, and a push to auto mode. Fable 5.2’s report card: #1 and $26.54 per task.
item.description: Cherny’s Nov 7 Hacker News response to the Apiiro settings.local.json findings and what Claude Code 2.1.321 actually fixed; Fable 5.2’s independent numbers from Artificial Analysis and Zapier; Adam Moore’s two-ticket $34 bill; Anthropic’s IPO roadshow; Gemini 4 Carbon GA; Hy4 weights; Muse Ember’s API.

item.title: No. 038: Anthropic says Fable 5.2 tops its coding benchmark — and still recommends Opus 5.5. Meta’s Muse Ember matches Haiku 5.5’s best score, Meta says.
item.description: Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 launch, with its own benchmarks set against Artificial Analysis’s intelligence, cost and speed measurements; Meta’s Muse Ember claims and its own lower coding score; Anthropic’s unverified Fermat statement.

item.title: No. 037: Goldman pulls Claude Code from its bankers and traders — Bloomberg’s report lands weeks before the bank takes Anthropic public. Nvidia’s board investigates Jensen Huang.
item.description: Bloomberg’s report that Goldman restricted Claude Code and GitHub coding tools to engineers, with the bank a lead underwriter on Anthropic’s reported IPO; Nvidia’s board investigation of Jensen Huang, separating board-confirmed facts from outlet allegations; frank chu’s planted-secrets scanner test; Langford’s scaling-philosophy detail; Declarative Dragging; Outlook’s DMARC enforcement.

item.title: No. 036: Claude Code’s “don’t ask again” saves your password with the command. 1,122 of those files are public.
item.description: Apiiro’s saved-secret findings on Claude Code’s settings.local.json, John Langford’s exit and the end of Microsoft’s AI Frontiers, Anthropic’s agent-memory dreaming post, the pre-Thanksgiving IPO push, MaxxBench and GitHub’s PR overview preview.

item.title: No. 035: Postman reverts the forced agent-plugin install: “we are reverting this change.” The terminal in your IDE is now one stable C library.
item.description: Postman’s revert after a week of backlash over silently installed agent plugins, libghostty 1.0’s stable C ABI with JetBrains’ reported 12.5M users, Anthropic’s IPO valuation slide, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash GA and the Jev+Opus routing claim.

item.title: No. 034: Claude Code puts the user’s email in outbound web requests — a fix is claimed, users can’t find it. sshole: locked SSH accounts take any long password.
item.description: The Claude Code email-in-User-Agent story and the claimed hard-to-find fix, the ten-year musl OpenSSH bypass found by agent swarms, Tencent’s Hy4 with weights pending, Inkling 2 Small closed-today-Apache-next-week and a $20K text-to-image claim.

item.title: No. 033: GitBook’s post-mortem documents the chain and softens the AI claim. OpenAI says its pipeline minted 948 Linux root exploits.
item.description: GitBook’s documented intrusion chain versus its AI inference, OpenAI’s 948-exploit Linux pipeline at $1,279 per exploit, Gemini’s training fine print for paying subscribers, the IEEE tech-debt analysis and Nvidia’s firmware tax.

item.title: No. 032: A developer catches Postman installing plugins into his other AI tools. GitBook says AI agents breached it.
item.description: Postman’s silent plugin installs and self-approved hook, GitBook’s AI-agent breach, Railway’s test agents attacking Primcloud, the Binance post-mortem and the Astra rebuttal-and-replication follow-up.

item.title: No. 031: GPT-6 Astra edits a model’s weights by hand. WorkOS says an AI attack framework hit its CRM.
item.description: Weight-space programming from MIT CSAIL, the WorkOS breach notice naming ARTEX, Anthropic’s Claude-over-payroll filing, OpenAI’s Pando Git backend and Subvocal’s silent-speech glasses.

item.title: No. 030: Someone had Claude build HackerTube for books overnight. A 9.8 Linux TCP bug is unpatched on Ubuntu.
item.description: HackerBooks and the one-night derivative, CVE-2026-98432’s distro patch gap, Calegari’s act-like-it-changed, the court AI that caught its own injection, a 13-stack framework benchmark and Postgres’s AI-delay receipts.

item.title: No. 029: One shared ChatGPT link was enough to take over your account. Malware now hires an LLM to rank you.
item.description: The ChatGPT share-link takeover and the MathLive mail slot, VOLTA’s LLM victim triage, Karpathy’s two-hour YouTube rebuild, a haiku from a TPU in orbit, Memdoor’s one-binary agent and Binance’s phased withdrawal restart.

item.title: No. 028: A maliciously modified Claude Code build on Cursor’s Marketplace planted an SSH backdoor. October breached nine AI platforms.
item.description: The Cursor Marketplace backdoor and the svc-telemetry self-check, Wiz’s Black October, Binance’s laptop root cause, Google’s Sleep framework, sanstun, and a Nintendo compiled into Qwen’s weights.

item.title: No. 027: Fifty signatures, 204 seconds, billions gone. Mistral opened its flagship.
item.description: The Binance hot-wallet drain and the EIP-7702 blind-signing hole, Mistral Large 4 open weights, the PAN-OS PHP2Shell chain, Fowler on LLM voice, a dreaming microcontroller, YC agent colonies and 27% more GPUs from the same racks.

item.title: No. 026: Apple’s git still trusts the compromised CA keys. Gemini 4 Carbon is out — for a gated few.
item.description: The eMudhra keys and your Mac, Gemini 4 Carbon, anti-LLM fingerprinting tripwires, Alpine’s GitLab rebuild, a 16-year-old UEFI bug, a CPU inside an LLM, a robot PCB factory and one defender’s week from hell.

item.title: No. 025: Anthropic answered OpenAI’s ETH manuscript with a refutation bylined Claude. The priority fight started the same afternoon.
item.description: The dueling ETH refutations, Ghostty 1.4, Genie 4, the removed Python JIT, Wikipedia’s cleanup crew, a 38-million-line Lean formalization, Survival LLM and fuzzing-versus-AI.

item.title: No. 024: Anthropic filed to go public. Then OpenAI claimed the Exponential Time Hypothesis is false.
item.description: The S-1, the ETH manuscript, Microsoft’s 60,000 buyout offers, Cohere’s Qwen sandbox catch, the failed C++26 ballot, a 4090 unlock and Entire.

item.title: No. 023: A dermatologist showed two frontier AIs 200 real skin cancers. A 10-year-old neural network beat them both.
item.description: The CNN-versus-LLM clinic test, the LLM price-collapse timeline, the banned TV hacker, ThinkRail, the Flock camera map, Overgrown and wordexp.

item.title: No. 022: Someone hid $500 of bitcoin on a server running a pre-PHP2Shell PHP and dared the internet to come take it.
item.description: The PHP2Shell bounty box, Dream-1’s zero-shot robots, the AI-payoff charts, Goose, the Tailworm audit, ThinkingCap and a video-editing skill.

item.title: No. 021: The compression library inside half the internet had a critical hole, and the fix took eight months to ship because nobody knew it was a security bug.
item.description: HTTP2Shell’s Brotli fire drill, Kimi K3.1 Pro, the Hexacon iPhone jailbreak, OpenAI’s no-internet training room, Dessa, 3d-model-anything and hatchzip.

item.title: No. 020: A certificate authority’s private key turned out to be the number 4. The board’s answer: quit the CA business entirely.
item.description: Anthropic’s formal-verification run, banks blocking AI agents at the login, WorldTUI, eMudhra’s exit, reylo, NCM and Snapintosh.

item.title: No. 019: The worst PHP bug in a decade was found by an AI on August 19. The patches, the exploits and the AI-written checker all landed yesterday.
item.description: PHP2Shell, a poisoned LiteLLM release, Claude Duet, a Railway breach, a test key shipped in mitmproxy and the boring patches that matter.
